premise: Woodpecker taps a rhythm on the big tree and Duckling quacks it back from the pond; little Acorn has no beak to join in and makes a wish, until Woodpecker says she can hop the beat.
inspiration: The call-and-response of folk songs, turned into a copycat game in which the smallest player finds her own sound and plays last.
lesson: There is a way for everyone to join in.

en-US.title: Tap, Quack, Boing!
en-US.text: {woodpecker:enter} Woodpecker flew to the big tree with bouncy wingbeats and clung to the trunk. [curious] Is anybody there? {woodpecker:live} {sfx:tap} Tap-tap-tap went his beak, and little chips flew. He listened… TAP! And he chirped. Down to the pond came {duckling:enter} Duckling, waddling. {sfx:quack} Quack-quack-quack… QUACK! {woodpecker:face surprised} A copycat! {woodpecker:face happy} [excited] Tap-tap! {duckling:hop} Quack-quack! Tap-tap-TAP! {duckling:shake} Quack-quack-QUACK! Then a tiny voice said, Can I play? It was {acorn:enter} Acorn, walking up on her little feet. {acorn:face sad} But I have no beak. {acorn:live hold} She clasped her hands, squeezed her eyes tight and wished. {woodpecker:pulse} Woodpecker thought. You have feet! You can HOP! {acorn:live resume} Acorn opened her eyes, threw up her arms and bounced. {sfx:boing} Boing! [laughs] Tap-tap, quack-quack, {all:face happy} {all:hop} BOING! {canvas:sunset 0.6 16s} They played copycat until the sun went down. Then Duckling {duckling:live hold} tucked his head under his wing. [whispers] Tap… quack… boing… goodnight.

es-ES.title: ¡Toc, cuac, boing!
es-ES.text: {woodpecker:enter} Pájaro carpintero voló hasta el árbol grande dando saltitos en el aire y se agarró al tronco. [curious] ¿Hay alguien ahí? {woodpecker:live} {sfx:tap} Toc-toc-toc, hizo su pico, y saltaron astillitas. Escuchó… ¡TOC! Y pió. A la charca llegó {duckling:enter} Patito, contoneándose. {sfx:quack} Cuac-cuac-cuac… ¡CUAC! {woodpecker:face surprised} ¡Un copión! {woodpecker:face happy} [excited] ¡Toc-toc! {duckling:hop} ¡Cuac-cuac! ¡Toc-toc-TOC! {duckling:shake} ¡Cuac-cuac-CUAC! Entonces una vocecita dijo: ¿Puedo jugar? Era {acorn:enter} Bellota, que llegaba andando con sus piececitos. {acorn:face sad} Pero yo no tengo pico. {acorn:live hold} Juntó las manitas, cerró los ojos muy fuerte y pidió un deseo. {woodpecker:pulse} Pájaro carpintero pensó. ¡Tienes pies! ¡Puedes SALTAR! {acorn:live resume} Bellota abrió los ojos, levantó los brazos y botó. {sfx:boing} ¡Boing! [laughs] Toc-toc, cuac-cuac, {all:face happy} {all:hop} ¡BOING! {canvas:sunset 0.6 16s} Jugaron a copiar hasta que se puso el sol. Entonces Patito {duckling:live hold} escondió la cabeza bajo el ala. [whispers] Toc… cuac… boing… buenas noches.

quack.prompt: four small cheerful duckling quacks, the last one louder

tap.prompt: a small woodpecker tapping lightly on a tree trunk, three quick soft taps

boing.prompt: one soft springy cartoon boing, playful and light
